headline: Cisco patched a Secure Email Gateway zero-day that hands attackers root on enterprise mail appliances, while ransomware crews joined the assault on VMware vCenter and a hijacked plugin maintainer backdoored 1,500 WordPress sites.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep landing on the appliances that sit at the network edge and the consoles that run everything behind it, from Cisco Secure Email Gateway to VMware vCenter to the Fortinet flaw that opened a Thai broadband provider, so a single unpatched box now costs an entire estate.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Hands Attackers Root

emerging_trends.text: China's spy chief cites Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5-Cyber as weapons, criminals rent an uncensored model called Luciferus on the Exploit forum, and Microsoft publishes rules meant to keep its own models out of operational attacks—AI capability and AI governance now move in the same week.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Beijing Flags US AI Models as Attack Tools

emerging_trends.text: Software distribution channels carry the payload: someone seized the maintainer site behind Admin Menu Editor Pro to ship backdoored updates, and mass scanners strip Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure keys out of Vite development servers left facing the internet.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Poisoned Plugins Backdoor WordPress and cPanel Hosts

topics.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Hands Attackers Root
topics.latest_developments: Cisco released the patch and confirmed active exploitation on September 15, 2026, detailing CVE-2026-76461 as a 9.8-rated failure to validate email parsing in AsyncOS versions 15.5, 16.0, and 16.5 that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands as root, published indicators of compromise for administrators to hunt with, and sharpened the SQL injection entry CISA posted to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog a day earlier.
topics.summary: Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliances handle inbound mail for large enterprises, and a crafted message reaches the underlying operating system with full privileges. Administrators should install the AsyncOS fix immediately and audit the appliances for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections.

sources.title: Cisco patches Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
Cisco Secure Email Gateway Flaw Exploited in the Wild, Enables Root Command Execution
Root RCE Zero-Day in Cisco Secure Email Gateway Under Active Exploitation
Cisco Secure Email Gateway vulnerability (CVE-2026-76461) in active exploitation

topics.title: Poisoned Plugins Backdoor WordPress and cPanel Hosts
topics.latest_developments: A threat actor compromised the website of the developer who maintains Admin Menu Editor Pro and pushed tampered updates to more than 200 customers, planting a hidden administrator account on 1,500 WordPress sites; hackers separately exploit a critical flaw in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture premium plugin to upload a PHP backdoor; Acronis disclosed a high-severity Linux privilege escalation bug in its backup plugin for cPanel, WebHost Manager, and Plesk that attackers may already exploit; and cPanel warned on September 14, 2026 that a LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise flaw lets the holder of one low-privilege hosting account take root on a shared server and reach every other site on the machine.
topics.summary: Shared hosting stacks pack thousands of customer sites onto single machines, and the plugins and control panels that manage them update automatically from vendor servers. Site owners should audit WordPress installs for administrator accounts nobody created, update the named plugins, and press hosting providers for their LiteSpeed and cPanel patch status.

sources.title: Malcious Admin Menu Editor Pro plugin backdoors 1,500 WordPress sites
Hackers target WordPress sites via third-party WooCommerce plugin
Acronis warns of actively exploited flaw in its cPanel backup plugin
LiteSpeed Enterprise Flaw Could Let One Hosting Account Gain Root Access on a Shared Server

topics.title: CenterPoint Energy Confirms Customer Data Theft
topics.latest_developments: CenterPoint Energy, the Houston electric and gas utility, confirmed on September 15, 2026 that attackers stole customer personal information, and it notified federal regulators after a hacker leaked the files on the dark web and claimed to hold 7.5 million customer records.
topics.summary: CenterPoint Energy delivers electricity and natural gas across Texas and several Midwest states, and the company limits the exposure it has confirmed to customer personal information. Customers should expect phishing that quotes real billing details and should watch their utility and financial accounts for fraud.

sources.title: CenterPoint Energy confirms customer data stolen in cyberattack
Texas Utility CenterPoint Energy Confirms Breach After Hacker Leaks Data
Electric and gas utility CenterPoint Energy warns of data breach after dark web post

topics.title: Beijing Flags US AI Models as Attack Tools
topics.latest_developments: China's spy chief named Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber on September 15, 2026 as signs of a disruptive upgrade in cyber capability that speeds vulnerability discovery and malware development; Sophos's Counter Threat Unit found a persona called Optimus_Prime advertising an uncensored AI subscription named Luciferus on the Exploit forum on August 24, 2026 as a substitute for jailbreaking ChatGPT or Claude; and OpenAI opened an investigation into research tying a swarm of its agents to the May 2026 attack on RubyGems.
topics.summary: Offensive AI has moved from research claim to market commodity, with state intelligence services citing commercial models as weapons and criminal forums selling purpose-built uncensored ones. Security teams should assume exploit development and phishing production now scale past what headcount used to allow.

sources.title: China spy chief points at US AI models in cyber threat warning
Uncensored AI sold on hacking forum as alternative to ChatGPT and Claude jailbreaks
OpenAI Investigates Report Linking AI Agents to RubyGems Attack

topics.title: Apple Ships Its Largest Patch Release Ever
topics.latest_developments: Apple shipped its annual operating system upgrade on September 14, 2026, fixing 261 vulnerabilities across its platforms by the SANS Internet Storm Center's count, roughly 200 of them in iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate 27, among them kernel flaws that lead to memory corruption, privilege escalation, system termination, and information leaks.
topics.summary: The release sets a record for Apple and lands amid the post-AI surge in vulnerability volume that has also driven record Microsoft and Adobe patch batches this month. Fleet managers should move iPhone, iPad, and Mac endpoints to the new releases and expect exploit writers to work backward from the kernel fixes.

sources.title: Apple Patches 200 Vulnerabilities With New iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate 27 Releases
Apple Updates Everything
MacOS 27 - First Boot

topics.title: Exposed Developer Servers Leak Cloud Credentials
topics.latest_developments: F5 Labs documented a mass-scanning campaign hunting internet-exposed Vite development servers to pull Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure credentials, configurations, and infrastructure state files out of them, and Sysdig separately clocked a human operator who turned a remote code execution flaw in a Marimo notebook into access on an SSH bastion host in eight seconds.
topics.summary: Development servers and notebooks hold live cloud keys and reach production networks, and administrators leave them open to the internet without authentication. Teams should pull Vite dev servers and Marimo notebooks off public addresses and rotate any cloud credential those hosts touched.

sources.title: Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers
Hackers target exposed Vite dev servers to steal AWS, Azure secrets
Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds

topics.title: Microsoft Sets Cyberattack Limits for Its AI Models
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft AI published the first draft of its Humanist AI Code of Conduct on September 15, 2026 and opened it to six weeks of public comment, drawing a line between defensive cyber research and operational attack capability and setting a chain of command and safety constraints for its models, and Microsoft separately agreed with the American Federation of Teachers to adopt privacy guardrails for the AI it puts in schools.
topics.summary: Microsoft plans to revise the code after the consultation and let the final version govern model development from 2027 onward, which makes it the first detailed vendor rulebook on where a frontier model stops helping with cyber operations. Security and procurement leaders should read the draft as the contractual baseline Microsoft will hold itself to and comment while the text stays open.

sources.title: Microsoft AI Code of Conduct Sets Cyberattack Boundaries, Chain of Command, Safety Constraints
Microsoft sets security and safety rules for its AI models
Microsoft Commits to Sweeping AI Privacy Rules for Students. Will Other Tech Giants Follow?

topics.title: Iran Uses Fake MRI Results to Phish Dissidents
topics.latest_developments: Cybersecurity agencies in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands jointly detailed Windows malware on September 15, 2026 that Iran's intelligence service steers over Telegram to copy a target's emails and chat messages, capture screenshots, and switch on the microphone, and the United Kingdom's National Cyber Security Centre described one lure in the campaign: fake MRI scan results sent to a person Tehran treats as an enemy of the regime.
topics.summary: Iranian operators build lures out of a target's personal circumstances, and medical results carry the urgency that defeats caution. Journalists, activists, and exiles with Iranian ties should verify any unexpected medical, legal, or immigration document through a second channel before opening it.

sources.title: Iranian cyber spies used fake MRI scan results to hack 'enemy of regime'
Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists

topics.title: Ransomware Gangs Join VMware vCenter Attacks
topics.latest_developments: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency warned security teams on September 15, 2026 that ransomware gangs have joined the ongoing exploitation of a critical remote code execution flaw in VMware vCenter that the vendor patched in July 2026.
topics.summary: vCenter runs the management plane for VMware virtual infrastructure, so one compromised server exposes every virtual machine beneath it, which is why extortion crews prize it. Administrators still holding the July release should apply it now and check vCenter logs for unrecognized administrative sessions.

sources.title: CISA: Critical VMware RCE flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs

topics.title: UTA0560 Plants GRIMWEDGE in NGOs
topics.latest_developments: Volexity reported on September 15, 2026 that the Chinese threat cluster it tracks as UTA0560 spear-phished several non-governmental organizations on September 1, 2026, chaining recently patched Google Chrome and Microsoft Windows flaws to drop a JavaScript backdoor the firm named GRIMWEDGE.
topics.summary: GRIMWEDGE arrives through a browser exploit chain that fires on a single spear-phishing click and leaves a JavaScript implant behind, the fourth Chrome and Windows chain researchers have documented this month. Organizations running Chrome should confirm they have the September updates on every endpoint.

sources.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE

business_politics.title: Senate Blocks the Crypto Market Structure Bill
business_politics.latest_developments: The Senate failed to advance the digital asset market structure bill on a procedural vote Tuesday, September 15, with Democrats withholding support until Congress limits President Trump's own cryptocurrency investments.
business_politics.summary: The legislation would have written the first federal rulebook for digital assets and carried them into the regulated financial system, and the industry spent record sums lobbying for it. Its defeat leaves exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and the banks serving them under the existing patchwork of Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement and state supervision.

sources.title: In a setback for the crypto industry, a bill that would have helped usher digital assets into the mainstream financial system failed to advance in Congress
Landmark US crypto bill fails as Senate splits over Trump ethics concerns

business_politics.title: Pentagon Watchdog Finds a Munitions Shortfall
business_politics.latest_developments: The Congressional Budget Office put the Pentagon's spending on the war with Iran at some $38 billion for its first months, in a report Tuesday, September 15, and estimated at least five years to replace the missile interceptors the fighting consumed, a longer and costlier bill than the $22 billion in ordnance the Defense Department inspector general counted.
business_politics.summary: The inspector general blamed industrial base bottlenecks for the slow pace of replacement, a constraint that shapes how long American forces can sustain strikes on Iranian targets and escorts through the Strait of Hormuz. Defense primes and their suppliers now face demand they cannot fill on the schedule the Pentagon wants.

sources.title: Iran war has left US with munitions 'shortfall', Pentagon watchdog says
The Pentagon spent some $38 billion in its first few months of the war with Iran

business_politics.title: Ten-Year Treasury Yield Tops 5%
business_politics.latest_developments: The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.04% Tuesday, September 15, the highest since 2007, and U.S. stocks fell with the Dow industrials leading the declines a day before the Federal Reserve decides on rates.
business_politics.summary: A global bond selloff has lifted long-term borrowing costs past levels last seen before the financial crisis, with traders pricing a Federal Reserve increase Wednesday, September 16, on the strength of Brent crude near $108 a barrel and record American diesel prices. The Wall Street Journal reported the same morning that regulators have begun scrutinizing the growing Treasury market footprint of hedge funds, a concentration that amplifies any dislocation.

sources.title: Stocks Decline as 10-Year Treasury Yield Hovers Near 5%
Ten-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2007

business_politics.title: Diesel Sets a Record at $6.27
business_politics.latest_developments: The average U.S. diesel price hit a record $6.27 a gallon Tuesday, September 15, oil futures rose again on the outage of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman traveled to Egypt for security talks with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi after Houthi drones and missiles injured 13 people in the kingdom.
business_politics.summary: Drones fired from Iraq knocked out the line that moves Saudi crude from the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea, and Houthi forces have seized territory commanding the Bab al-Mandeb corridor, leaving the crown prince fighting on two fronts. American manufacturers report a fresh burst of supply chain cost inflation from the Iran war, tariffs, and AI-driven component scarcity.

business_politics.title: Kyiv and Moscow Strike Energy Targets After Truce Claim
business_politics.latest_developments: Russia and Ukraine traded aerial strikes overnight into Tuesday, September 15, hitting gas stations in Kyiv and energy infrastructure in the southeastern Zaporizhzhia region one day after President Trump announced the two sides had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy systems, and Denmark called a Russian warship reckless for firing flares past one of its helicopters over the Baltic Sea.
business_politics.summary: Trump said Monday, September 14, that Moscow and Kyiv would spare energy infrastructure, an announcement that surprised Ukrainian officials, and he had pressed Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian refineries that he blames for record diesel prices. The exchange of strikes leaves the oil and refined-product markets without the relief a genuine energy truce would supply.

sources.title: Russia, Ukraine Trade Aerial Strikes After Trump's Claim of Truce
Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter over Baltic Sea

business_politics.title: Supreme Court Blocks Trump's Mail Ballot Rules
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump attacked the justices publicly Tuesday, September 15, saying "these are not the people I interviewed," after the Supreme Court rejected his administration's mail-ballot requirements Monday night in an unsigned order from which Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented.
business_politics.summary: Trump's executive order would have imposed fresh requirements on mail voting weeks before the November congressional elections, with voting already underway in some states; a federal appeals court blocked it September 10 and the administration sought emergency relief. Election administrators had warned that implementing new rules this late would throw the midterms into a scramble.

sources.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail-in ballot restrictions for midterms
The Supreme Court blocked the Trump administration from imposing new requirements for mail ballots, averting what officials warned would have been a crisis in the midterm elections

business.title: County Council Moves to Bar Data Centers From County Property
business.latest_developments: The Allegheny County Council Committee on Sustainability and Green Initiatives voted unanimously Tuesday, September 15, to advance an amended measure prohibiting data centers of 25 megawatts or more from using county-owned buildings or land.
business.summary: The bill now goes to the full Allegheny County Council, and it would close county property to projects on the scale of the Homer City Energy Campus in Indiana County and Project Phoenix in Beaver County. Municipalities around the region are fielding their own inquiries, among them Elizabeth Township, where commissioners disclosed this week that a developer has approached them about a data center.

sources.title: Allegheny County Council committee votes to advance ban on large-scale data centers on county property

business.title: PennSTART Test Track Draws Federal Attention
business.latest_developments: WTAE reported Tuesday, September 15, that federal transportation officials have taken an interest in the PennSTART test track going up in Westmoreland County, which opens in early 2027.
business.summary: PennSTART gives Western Pennsylvania a closed course for training first responders and testing autonomous vehicles, work that now travels to facilities in other states. Construction continues toward an opening in the first months of 2027.

sources.title: Western Pa. test track grabs attention of federal transportation officials

business.title: CooksonPeirce Moves to 11 Stanwix
business.latest_developments: WPXI reported Tuesday, September 15, that the money management firm CooksonPeirce will leave 555 Grant Street for 11 Stanwix Street in downtown Pittsburgh just ahead of Halloween.
business.summary: CooksonPeirce has kept its headquarters at 555 Grant Street for more than two decades and now sets a move-in date at 11 Stanwix Street, on the western edge of the Golden Triangle. The relocation adds another tenant shift to a downtown office market working through vacancies and conversions.

sources.title: CooksonPeirce relocating downtown Pittsburgh headquarters, sets move-in date

business.title: Developers Circle Larimer's Vacant Parcels
business.latest_developments: Urban Redevelopment Authority director Zober told the URA board at its September meeting, WPXI reported Tuesday, September 15, that the request for information the agency issued in June on two collections of open parcels in Larimer has drawn strong interest.
business.summary: The URA controls scattered vacant land in Larimer, the East End neighborhood where public agencies have spent a decade assembling sites for housing, and the June request asked builders what they would put there. The board heard the update the same month it approved $4.85 million in loans to Woda Cooper Cos. for a downtown apartment conversion.

sources.title: Redevelopment director reports strong interest in East End housing sites

business.title: 100 Employers at the Monroeville Career Fair
business.latest_developments: KDKA's Jessica Riley reported Tuesday, September 15, that the PA CareerLink Awareness Day career fair returns to Monroeville on Wednesday, September 16, with upwards of 100 employers and job resources in one place.
business.summary: PA CareerLink, the state and county workforce system that runs job centers across Allegheny County, gathers hiring employers and training providers for the day. The fair lands as white-collar hiring slows and regional trade schools report enrollment increases.

sources.title: PA CareerLink Awareness Day career fair returning to Monroeville

business.title: Superloads Roll Wednesday
business.latest_developments: KDKA reported Tuesday, September 15, that the first superload deliveries to Pennsylvania data center construction sites begin Wednesday, September 16, with each haul running the size of a Boeing 777 with its wings tucked in.
business.summary: The hauls carry equipment weighing as much as 380 tons from the Armstrong Terminals in Gilpin to the data center project near Homer City in Indiana County, where more than 1,800 construction workers are already at work on the Homer City Energy Campus. The loads slipped past two earlier announced start dates.

sources.title: Superload deliveries to Pennsylvania data centers expected to get underway tomorrow

business.title: Hispanic Chamber Opens New Programs for Entrepreneurs
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine reported Tuesday, September 15, that the Pennsylvania Metropolitan Area Hispanic Chamber of Commerce is launching programs and resources for Hispanic business owners as Hispanic Heritage Month begins.
business.summary: Hispanic Heritage Month runs September 15, the independence anniversary for Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua, through October 15, and the chamber marks it with galas, festivals, and support work for Hispanic-owned businesses across the Pittsburgh region.

sources.title: New Programs Support Hispanic Business Owners During Hispanic Heritage Month

business.title: Liquor Money as Growth Money
business.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Brandon McGinley argued Tuesday, September 15, that Pennsylvania should study how Ohio turns state liquor sales profits into economic development through JobsOhio.
business.summary: Ohio pledges the profits of its state liquor enterprise to JobsOhio, the private nonprofit that recruits employers and readies industrial sites, giving the state a dedicated stream of deal money. Pennsylvania runs its own liquor stores through the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board and pays for site preparation out of Governor Josh Shapiro's PA SITES program, which competes for general fund dollars every budget cycle.

sources.title: Brandon McGinley: How Ohio juices growth with liquor sales, and what we can learn from it

business.title: KLVN Closes and the Gobblerito Turns 20
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Tuesday, September 15, that KLVN Coffee Lab has closed and that Mad Mex's Gobblerito reaches its 20th year, alongside fresh word on Penn Brewery, Acrisure Stadium concessions, and Jackworth Ginger Beer.
business.summary: KLVN Coffee Lab shuts its doors as the Gobblerito, the Thanksgiving-dinner burrito that Mad Mex sells each fall, marks two decades on the menu. Penn Brewery, the Troy Hill brewer that filed for bankruptcy five months ago, has landed new owners.

business.title: Riverfront Theater Moves Downtown
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 15, that Riverfront Theater Company has left Aspinwall for a space in Pittsburgh's Cultural District, keeping its name.
business.summary: Riverfront Theater Company built its audience in the Allegheny River borough of Aspinwall and now joins the concentration of stages in the Cultural District downtown. The move puts a small producing company inside the same blocks as the Benedum Center and the Byham Theater.

sources.title: Riverfront Theater Company relocates from Aspinwall to Pittsburgh's Cultural District

around_town.title: Allegheny County's Pension Hole Deepens
around_town.latest_developments: The Allegheny County treasurer rejected a call to resign Tuesday, September 15, as the county's pension shortfall widened, WPXI reported.
around_town.summary: The county retirement board released an analysis in July showing Allegheny County would have to contribute more than $100 million a year to return the pension fund to solvency. The treasurer sits on that board, which manages retirement money for thousands of county workers.

sources.title: Treasurer rejects call to resign as Allegheny pension problems grow

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Records a Fourth Measles Death
around_town.latest_developments: A Mifflin County coroner reported the state's fourth death this year from complications of measles, WTAE reported Tuesday, September 15.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania leads the country in confirmed measles cases, with state health officials counting 676 on September 11. The earlier deaths took two infants and a 40-year-old Jefferson County woman who carried several chronic respiratory conditions.

sources.title: Pennsylvania sees 4th death from measles, state officials say

around_town.title: Penn Hills Removes Its Police Chief
around_town.latest_developments: Penn Hills removed police Chief Jason Bonace from his job, the Post-Gazette and WPXI reported Tuesday, September 15, and the municipality has given no reason for it.
around_town.summary: Bonace ran the police department in Penn Hills, the Allegheny County municipality east of Pittsburgh. Municipal leaders and members of the department have split over the termination, and neither side has explained publicly what prompted it.

sources.title: Penn Hills' police chief was removed from his position. Officials aren't saying why.
Penn Hills municipal leaders, law enforcement divided over police chief termination

around_town.title: UPMC Children's Makes the National Honor Roll
around_town.latest_developments: U.S. News & World Report placed UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh on its Best Children's Hospital Honor Roll for 2026-27, among the nation's top 10 pediatric hospitals, WPXI reported Tuesday, September 15.
around_town.summary: The Lawrenceville hospital ties for first in Pennsylvania and first in the mid-Atlantic region, and it earned national rankings in all 11 pediatric specialties the magazine evaluates. UPMC Children's serves as the region's referral center for complex pediatric care.

sources.title: UPMC Children's Hospital recognized among nation's top 10 pediatric hospitals

around_town.title: Elizabeth Township Approves Wells Near a School
around_town.latest_developments: Elizabeth Township commissioners approved EQT's fracked gas wells near a township school over resident objections, PublicSource reported Tuesday, September 15, and disclosed that a developer has approached them about a data center.
around_town.summary: Residents of the Allegheny County township pressed the commissioners to reject the drilling on grounds of proximity to the school, and the board approved it anyway. The commissioners offered few details on the data center inquiry and promised a public information session.

sources.title: Elizabeth Township OKs fracked wells near a school despite resident concern

around_town.title: Salinetro Sends $200,000 to a Mt. Washington Rec Center
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Councilwoman Kim Salinetro secured $200,000 on Tuesday, September 15, for a Mt. Washington recreation center that has operated without city funding for nearly two decades.
around_town.summary: Salinetro becomes the third Pittsburgh City Council member to direct money to an underfunded neighborhood recreation center, a pattern of members using their own capital allocations to prop up facilities the city budget stopped carrying. The Mt. Washington center has run on outside money since the mid-2000s.

sources.title: 3rd Pittsburgh council member gets $200K for an underfunded rec center

around_town.title: Hulton Road Stays Closed Another Month
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation extended the slide repair on Hulton Road in Plum Borough, keeping the road closed around the clock for another month, WPXI reported Tuesday, September 15.
around_town.summary: Crews are stabilizing a hillside slide along Hulton Road, the Plum Borough route that carries traffic toward the Allegheny River crossing at Oakmont. Drivers have already lived with a full closure and now face roughly four more weeks of detours.

sources.title: Hulton Road to remain closed for another month for extended slide repair

around_town.title: Impact Days Wednesday and Thursday
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE held Wednesday, September 16, and Thursday, September 17, as Impact Days in its Tuesday afternoon update, September 15, after a warm, dry Tuesday with highs in the upper 70s and low 80s and humidity climbing through the evening.
around_town.summary: Tuesday stays dry across the Pittsburgh area, and the next system arrives midweek with rain heavy enough for the stations to flag two straight days. The region has taken repeated flooding this summer, most recently in Washington County and along Wildwood Road in Hampton Township.

around_town.title: Pitcairn Council Keeps Its ICE Agreement
around_town.latest_developments: Pitcairn Borough Council voted 5-2 on Monday, September 14, against a resolution to terminate the borough police department's cooperation agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
around_town.summary: Pitcairn entered the 287(g) agreement, which deputizes local officers to perform federal immigration functions, without public input or a council vote, and residents filled a heated meeting to demand that the council undo it. The vote runs opposite the direction taken in Stowe Township, where commissioners rescinded their own 287(g) agreement earlier this month.

around_town.title: 1,400 Comments on Paid Parental Leave
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Tuesday, September 15, that Allegheny County collected about 1,400 public comments on its paid parental leave proposal, a record for the county, and that the tally shows broad support, a deep split, and appetite for changes to the bill.
around_town.summary: The legislation before Allegheny County Council would give county employees 18 weeks of paid parental leave, a signature item for County Executive Sara Innamorato as she seeks reelection, and the Council's health committee held a public hearing on it September 10. Residents now get another window to weigh in on possible amendments.

sources.title: 1,400 paid parental leave comments show support, deep split, room for change

around_town.title: Plum Backs Clover Commons Residents
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 15, that the land-rent increase driving the Clover Commons protest runs 11%, and that Plum Borough Council has answered the residents with a resolution urging the Pennsylvania legislature to act, while the TribLive editorial board pressed the state Senate the same day to move on manufactured home protections.
around_town.summary: Nearly 60 residents of Clover Commons, a manufactured home community in Plum for people 55 and older, marched through their own streets over the increase and asked state senators to pass House Bill 1250. Homeowners in such communities own the house and rent the ground beneath it, which leaves them exposed when an owner raises the rent.

events.summary: Luke Bryan brings his Farm Tour to 1846 Farms in Unity Township, near Latrobe, on Thursday, September 17, the sort of one-night show the country singer stages in working farm fields each fall. KDKA's reports did not state a start time or ticket prices.

events.summary: Penn Brewery, the German-style brewery on Pittsburgh's North Side that filed for bankruptcy earlier this year and has since landed new owners, pours hefeweizen and books polka for Oktoberfest this weekend. KDKA's segment gave no hours or admission price.

sources.title: Oktoberfest returns to Pittsburgh

events.summary: Chesney returns to Acrisure Stadium on Pittsburgh's North Shore, the football stadium he has filled repeatedly on stadium tours, for a Memorial Day weekend date in May 2027. events.latest_developments: TribLive previewed the 16th Pittsburgh International Jazz Festival on Tuesday, September 15, and Pittsburgh Magazine's weekend list the same day leads with it; the festival runs Thursday, September 17, through Sunday, September 20, in downtown Pittsburgh.

events.title: Flight 93 Chalk Portraits in Somerset
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 15, that the chalk portraits of the 40 Flight 93 passengers and crew will stay on view in Somerset through Sunday, September 20.
events.summary: Artists drew the portraits in chalk for the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks, and organizers are preserving them in Somerset, the Somerset County seat about 15 miles from the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township. Visitors can see them through Sunday, September 20.

sources.title: Chalk portraits of Flight 93 crew and passengers will be preserved until Sunday in Somerset

events.title: Film on Film at Row House Hollywood
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper profiled projectionist Katerina Sarandou on Tuesday, September 15, who has run the booth at Row House Hollywood since the theater's first screening.
events.summary: Row House Hollywood programs 35mm and 70mm prints for audiences that want movies projected the pre-digital way, and Sarandou threads and runs every one of them. The theater is the second house from the Row House team, which started with Row House Cinema in Lawrenceville.

sources.title: Katerina Sarandou revives the art of film projection at Row House Hollywood

around_teams.title: Roethlisberger and Holmes Revisit the Super Bowl Catch
around_teams.latest_developments: Footbahlin posted episode 139 Tuesday evening, September 15, with Ben Roethlisberger interviewing Santonio Holmes for the first time about the Super Bowl XLIII touchdown and the Steelers' Week 1 win.
around_teams.summary: Holmes made the toe-tap catch in the corner of the end zone that won Super Bowl XLIII, and on Roethlisberger's show he walks through what he read before the snap and the offseason corner-route repetitions behind it. The two then took up the opening victory over the Atlanta Falcons.

sources.title: Big Ben & Santonio Holmes talk The Catch That Won A Super Bowl, Steelers Week 1 Win and More! Ep 139

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Counts the Snaps
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler went through the Steelers' Week 1 snap counts player by player on SNR Drive Tuesday, September 15, took a call from broadcaster Rob King, and ran the league's Week 2 power rankings.
around_teams.summary: SNR Drive is the Steelers' daily show on the club's channel, and Williamson, a former NFL scout, spends the Tuesday episode rewatching the opener against the Atlanta Falcons. Pittsburgh plays at the New England Patriots Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Giving Our Tuesday Rewatch Thoughts | SNR Drive (Sept.15) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Pirates Spend Clemente Day in the Neighborhoods
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates handed out food, visited local schools, and cleaned up community fields for Roberto Clemente Day on Tuesday, September 15, with Brandon Lowe wearing No. 21 as the club's nominee for the Roberto Clemente Award.
around_teams.summary: Major League Baseball names one player per club for the award, which honors community work and carries the name of the outfielder who played 18 seasons in Pittsburgh. Lowe has drawn the nomination before and told the Post-Gazette it means more to him in a Pirates uniform.

sources.title: The Pirates distribute food, visit local schools and clean up community fields on Roberto Clemente Day

around_teams.title: Beazley Takes Pirates Questions in the Final Weeks
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette beat writer Colin Beazley held his Pirates chat Tuesday, September 15, fielding reader questions as the club plays out a season its playoff hopes have left.
around_teams.summary: Beazley covers the Pirates for the Post-Gazette and takes readers' questions weekly; his colleagues argued this week that the front office's trade deadline choices should haunt it, while the organization's best hitting prospects, outfielder Edward Florentino among them, carry a playoff run at the Greensboro affiliate.

sources.title: Colin Beazley's Pirates chat transcript: 09.15.26

around_teams.title: Week 1 Grades Split Watt and Metcalf
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its Week 1 grades Tuesday, September 15, calling T.J. Watt's performance that of a superstar and marking down receiver DK Metcalf.
around_teams.summary: Watt's pick-six against the Atlanta Falcons decided the Steelers' season opener, and Alex Highsmith's late sack closed it out, while Metcalf, acquired to stretch the field for quarterback Aaron Rodgers, drew the harshest review of the afternoon. The offense, hemmed in by penalties, told reporters it sits close to hitting the big plays it drew up.

sources.title: Steelers Week 1 grades: T.J. Watt played like a superstar. DK Metcalf definitely did not.

around_teams.title: Dan Rooney Talks German Plans on Männer aus Stahl
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted the new season opener of their German-language podcast Männer aus Stahl on Tuesday, September 15, with Vice President of Strategy Dan Rooney discussing the club's plans for its German fan base.
around_teams.summary: ProSieben host Christoph "Icke" Dommisch interviews Rooney, a member of the family that founded the Steelers, about the team's first game with Borussia Dortmund, its flag football camp in Germany, and German food. The Steelers hold marketing rights in Germany and have built a following there.

sources.title: STEELERS-VIZEPRÄSIDENT VERRÄT DEUTSCHLAND-PLÄNE BEI ICKE AM MIKRO

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Turns the Page to New England
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Monday's SNR Drive, posted September 14 on the Steelers' channel, reviewing the Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons and head coach Mike McCarthy's Monday news conference, and the club began promoting Week 2 at the New England Patriots, Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.
around_teams.summary: SNR Drive is the Steelers' daily radio and video show, and Williamson, a former NFL scout, works through the tape and the coach's remarks with Uhler each weekday. McCarthy, in his first season running the team, met reporters Monday to open preparation for the trip to Foxborough.

sources.title: Recapping Yesterday's 20-13 Win Against The Falcons | SNR Drive (Sept.14) | Pittsburgh Steelers
Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 2 at New England Patriots) | Pittsburgh Steelers

team_usa.title: Fredette Leaves USA Basketball to Play Again
team_usa.latest_developments: Jimmer Fredette stepped down Tuesday, September 15, as managing director of USA Basketball's men's 3x3 program to resume his own playing career, with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in view.
team_usa.summary: Fredette played 3x3 for the United States at the 2024 Paris Olympics and then took over the front office of the men's program, which selects and prepares the American 3x3 team for World Cups and the Games. USA Basketball now needs a replacement in that job.

sources.title: Fredette leaves USA Basketball to resume 3x3 playing career

team_usa.title: Morgan and Dunn Press FIFA on the U20 World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: More than a dozen current and former players, among them World Cup winners Alex Morgan and Crystal Dunn of the United States and Brazil's Marta, sent an open letter to FIFA on Tuesday, September 15, asking it to align the Under-20 Women's World Cup with the international match calendar.
team_usa.summary: Clubs owe no obligation to release players for tournaments staged outside FIFA's official windows, which leaves teenagers choosing between their national teams and their employers. The American under-20 program feeds the senior United States women's team, and the letter asks FIFA to remove that choice.

sources.title: Morgan, Marta lead chorus of players seeking U20 WWC change

team_usa.title: Diego Luna Faces Months Out With a Knee Injury
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday, September 15, that Real Salt Lake and United States midfielder Diego Luna will miss months with a knee injury and will likely undergo an arthroscopic procedure to determine its extent.
team_usa.summary: Luna has been a fixture in the United States men's national team pool and plays his club soccer for Real Salt Lake in Major League Soccer. The layoff takes him out of contention for the roster the U.S. men are set to announce this week.

sources.title: Sources: USMNT's Luna (knee) sent to be sidelined for months

team_usa.title: Colombia Courts Alexander Shaw
team_usa.latest_developments: A source told ESPN on Tuesday, September 15, that Colombia has contacted Inter Miami midfielder Alexander Shaw, who played for the United States under-20 team in this year's Concacaf tournament, setting up a fight over his international future.
team_usa.summary: Shaw holds dual nationality, and a player who has appeared only in youth competition may still switch federations before committing at the senior level. The United States developed him through its under-20 program, and Colombia now aims to pull him the other way.

sources.title: Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Alexander Shaw

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: OpenAI Ads, Amazon Ads in ChatGPT, Walmart to Accept Apple Pay
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues that advertising inside ChatGPT is already working and that it hands Amazon an answer to the problem chatbots pose to its retail search business. He reads Walmart's decision to accept Apple Pay as proof that fighting an entrenched standard costs more than joining it.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands
reading.summary: Zitron contends that the speculative case about future superintelligence distracts from the concrete harm the people running today's AI companies are doing with the technology they already control.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport dismisses the prospect of self-improving superintelligence as a story the industry tells itself, writing in response to Anthropic employees who said publicly that their work could kill billions. He argues the pursuit still does damage through the money, energy, and social disruption it consumes along the way.
